ESV.1: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Gerar to Abimelech king of the Philistines.
ESV.2: And the LORD appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land of which I shall tell you.
ESV.3: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and will bless you, for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.
ESV.4: I will multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and will give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,
ESV.5: because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
ESV.7: When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, “She is my sister,” for he feared to say, “My wife,” thinking, “lest the men of the place should kill me because of Rebekah,” because she was attractive in appearance.
ESV.8: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out of a window and saw Isaac laughing with  Rebekah his wife.
ESV.9: So Abimelech called Isaac and said, “Behold, she is your wife. How then could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I thought, ‘Lest I die because of her.’”
ESV.10: Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”
ESV.11: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.”
ESV.12: And Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold. The LORD blessed him,
ESV.13: and the man became rich, and gained more and more until he became very wealthy.
ESV.14: He had possessions of flocks and herds and many servants, so that the Philistines envied him.
ESV.15: (Now the Philistines had stopped and filled with earth all the wells that his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father.)
ESV.16: And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.”
ESV.17: So Isaac departed from there and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.
ESV.18: And Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped after the death of Abraham. And he gave them the names that his father had given them.
ESV.19: But when Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of spring water,
ESV.20: the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Esek,  because they contended with him.
ESV.21: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that also, so he called its name Sitnah.
ESV.22: And he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. So he called its name Rehoboth,  saying, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”
ESV.23: From there he went up to Beersheba.
ESV.24: And the LORD appeared to him the same night and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Fear not, for I am with you and will bless you and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham's sake.”
ESV.25: So he built an altar there and called upon the name of the LORD and pitched his tent there. And there Isaac's servants dug a well.
ESV.26: When Abimelech went to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army,
ESV.27: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and have sent me away from you?”
ESV.28: They said, “We see plainly that the LORD has been with you. So we said, let there be a sworn pact between us, between you and us, and let us make a covenant with you,
ESV.29: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and have done to you nothing but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.”
ESV.30: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
ESV.31: In the morning they rose early and exchanged oaths. And Isaac sent them on their way, and they departed from him in peace.
ESV.32: That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well that they had dug and said to him, “We have found water.”
ESV.33: He called it Shibah;  therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
ESV.34: When Esau was forty years old, he took Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite to be his wife, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite,
ESV.35: and they made life bitter  for Isaac and Rebekah.

NASB.1: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the previous famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. So Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech king of the Philistines.
NASB.2: The LORD appeared to him and said, 'Do not go down to Egypt; stay in the land of which I shall tell you.
NASB.3: 'Sojourn in this land and I will be with you and bless you, for to you and to your descendants I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to your father Abraham.
NASB.4: 'I will multiply your descendants as the stars of heaven, and will give your descendants all these lands; and by your descendants all the nations of the earth shall be blessed;
NASB.5: because Abraham obeyed Me and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes and My laws.'
NASB.7: When the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, 'She is my sister,' for he was afraid to say, 'my wife,' [thinking], 'the men of the place might kill me on account of Rebekah, for she is beautiful.'
NASB.8: It came about, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out through a window, and saw, and behold, Isaac was caressing his wife Rebekah.
NASB.9: Then Abimelech called Isaac and said, 'Behold, certainly she is your wife! How then did you say, 'She is my sister '?' And Isaac said to him, 'Because I said, 'I might die on account of her.''

NASB.11: So Abimelech charged all the people, saying, 'He who touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.'
NASB.12: Now Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him,
NASB.13: and the man became rich, and continued to grow richer until he became very wealthy;
NASB.14: for he had possessions of flocks and herds and a great household, so that the Philistines envied him.
NASB.15: Now all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped up by filling them with earth.
NASB.16: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, 'Go away from us, for you are too powerful for us.'
NASB.17: And Isaac departed from there and camped in the valley of Gerar, and settled there.
NASB.18: Then Isaac dug again the wells of water which had been dug in the days of his father Abraham, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham; and he gave them the same names which his father had given them.
NASB.19: But when Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of flowing water,

NASB.21: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over it too, so he named it Sitnah.
NASB.22: He moved away from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it; so he named it Rehoboth, for he said, 'At last the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.'

NASB.25: So he built an altar there and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there; and there Isaac's servants dug a well.
NASB.26: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with his adviser Ahuzzath and Phicol the commander of his army.
NASB.27: Isaac said to them, 'Why have you come to me, since you hate me and have sent me away from you?'
NASB.28: They said, 'We see plainly that the LORD has been with you; so we said, 'Let there now be an oath between us, [even] between you and us, and let us make a covenant with you,
NASB.29: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and have done to you nothing but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.''
NASB.30: Then he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
NASB.31: In the morning they arose early and exchanged oaths; then Isaac sent them away and they departed from him in peace.
NASB.32: Now it came about on the same day, that Isaac's servants came in and told him about the well which they had dug, and said to him, 'We have found water.'
NASB.33: So he called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
NASB.34: When Esau was forty years old he married Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite;
NASB.35: and they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.

NKJV.1: There was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, in Gerar.
NKJV.2: Then the LORD appeared to him and said: “Do not go down to Egypt; live in the land of which I shall tell you.
NKJV.3: Dwell in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and your descendants I give all these lands, and I will perform the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
NKJV.4: And I will make your descendants multiply as the stars of heaven; I will give to your descendants all these lands; and in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed;
NKJV.5: because Abraham obeyed My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.”
NKJV.7: And the men of the place asked about his wife. And he said, “She is my sister”; for he was afraid to say, “She is my wife,” because he thought, “lest the men of the place kill me for Rebekah, because she is beautiful to behold.”
NKJV.8: Now it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked through a window, and saw, and there was Isaac, showing endearment to Rebekah his wife.
NKJV.9: Then Abimelech called Isaac and said, “Quite obviously she is your wife; so how could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I said, ‘Lest I die on account of her.’ ”
NKJV.10: And Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might soon have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us.”
NKJV.11: So Abimelech charged all his people, saying, “He who touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.”
NKJV.12: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and reaped in the same year a hundredfold; and the LORD blessed him.
NKJV.13: The man began to prosper, and continued prospering until he became very prosperous;
NKJV.14: for he had possessions of flocks and possessions of herds and a great number of servants. So the Philistines envied him.
NKJV.15: Now the Philistines had stopped up all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, and they had filled them with earth.
NKJV.16: And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.”
NKJV.17: Then Isaac departed from there and pitched his tent in the Valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
NKJV.18: And Isaac dug again the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham. He called them by the names which his father had called them.
NKJV.19: Also Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, and found a well of running water there.
NKJV.20: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Esek, because they quarreled with him.
NKJV.21: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also. So he called its name Sitnah.
NKJV.22: And he moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. So he called its name Rehoboth, because he said, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”
NKJV.23: Then he went up from there to Beersheba.
NKJV.24: And the LORD appeared to him the same night and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham; do not fear, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for My servant Abraham’s sake.”
NKJV.25: So he built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD, and he pitched his tent there; and there Isaac’s servants dug a well.
NKJV.26: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath, one of his friends, and Phichol the commander of his army.
NKJV.27: And Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, since you hate me and have sent me away from you?”
NKJV.28: But they said, “We have certainly seen that the LORD is with you. So we said, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, between you and us; and let us make a covenant with you,
NKJV.29: that you will do us no harm, since we have not touched you, and since we have done nothing to you but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.’ ”
NKJV.30: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
NKJV.31: Then they arose early in the morning and swore an oath with one another; and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
NKJV.32: It came to pass the same day that Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well which they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.”
NKJV.33: So he called it Shebah. Therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
NKJV.34: When Esau was forty years old, he took as wives Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
NKJV.35: And they were a grief of mind to Isaac and Rebekah.

AMP.1: Now there was a famine in the land [of Canaan], besides the previous famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. So Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech king of the Philistines.
AMP.2: The LORD appeared to him and said, "Do not go down to Egypt; stay in the land of which I will tell you.
AMP.3: Live temporarily [as a resident] in this land and I will be with you and will bless and favor you, for I will give all these lands to you and to your descendants, and I will establish and carry out the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
AMP.4: I will make your descendants multiply as the stars of the heavens, and will give to your descendants all these lands; and by your descendants shall all the nations of the earth be blessed,
AMP.5: because Abraham listened to and obeyed My voice and [consistently] kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws."
AMP.7: The men of the place asked him about his wife, and he said, "She is my sister," for he was afraid to say, "my wife"—thinking, "the men of the place might kill me on account of Rebekah, since she is very beautiful."
AMP.8: It happened when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out of a window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.
AMP.9: Then Abimelech called Isaac and said, "See here, Rebekah is in fact your wife! How did you [dare to] say to me, 'She is my sister'?" And Isaac said to him, "Because I thought I might be killed because of her [desirability]."
AMP.10: Abimelech said, "What is this that you have done to us? One of the men [among our people] might easily have been intimate with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us [before God]."
AMP.11: Then Abimelech commanded all his people, "Whoever touches this man [Isaac] or his wife [Rebekah] shall without exception be put to death."
AMP.12: Then Isaac planted [seed] in that land [as a farmer] and reaped in the same year a hundred times [as much as he had planted], and the LORD blessed and favored him.
AMP.13: And the man [Isaac] became great and gained more and more until he became very wealthy and extremely distinguished;
AMP.14: he owned flocks and herds and a great household [with a number of servants], and the Philistines envied him.
AMP.15: Now all the wells which his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped up by filling them with dirt.
AMP.16: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, "Go away from here, because you are far too powerful for us."
AMP.17: So Isaac left that region and camped in the Valley of Gerar, and settled there.
AMP.18: Now Isaac again dug [and reopened] the wells of water which had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, because the Philistines had filled them up [with dirt] after the death of Abraham; and he gave the wells the same names that his father had given them.
AMP.19: But when Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of flowing [spring] water,
AMP.20: the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours!" So Isaac named the well Esek (quarreling), because they quarreled with him.
AMP.21: Then his servants dug another well, and they quarreled over that also, so Isaac named it Sitnah (enmity).
AMP.22: He moved away from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over that one; so he named it Rehoboth (broad places), saying, "For now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be prosperous in the land."
AMP.23: Then he went up from there to Beersheba.
AMP.24:
The LORD appeared to him the same night and said,
"I am the God of Abraham your father;
Do not be afraid, for I am with you.
I will bless and favor you, and multiply your descendants,
For the sake of My servant Abraham."
AMP.25: So Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD [in prayer]. He pitched his tent there; and there Isaac's servants dug a well.
AMP.26: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath, his [close friend and confidential] adviser, and Phicol, the commander of his army.
AMP.27: Isaac said to them, "Why have you [people] come to me, since you hate me and have sent me away from you?"
AMP.28: They said, "We see clearly that the LORD has been with you; so we said, 'There should now be an oath between us [with a curse for the one who breaks it], that is, between you and us, and let us make a covenant (binding agreement, solemn promise) with you,
AMP.29: that you will not harm us, just as we have not touched you and have done nothing but good to you and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed and favored of the LORD!'"
AMP.30: Then Isaac held a [formal] banquet (covenant feast) for them, and they ate and drank.
AMP.31: They got up early in the morning and swore oaths [pledging to do nothing but good to each other]; and Isaac sent them on their way and they left him in peace.
AMP.32: Now on the same day, Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug, saying, "We have found water."
AMP.33: So he named the well Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
AMP.34: When Esau was forty years old he married Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite as his wives;
AMP.35: and they were a source of grief to [Esau's parents] Isaac and Rebekah.

NLT.1: A severe famine now struck the land, as had happened before in Abraham’s time. So Isaac moved to Gerar, where Abimelech, king of the Philistines, lived.
NLT.2: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt, but do as I tell you.
NLT.3: Live here as a foreigner in this land, and I will be with you and bless you. I hereby confirm that I will give all these lands to you and your descendants, just as I solemnly promised Abraham, your father.
NLT.4: I will cause your descendants to become as numerous as the stars of the sky, and I will give them all these lands. And through your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
NLT.5: I will do this because Abraham listened to me and obeyed all my requirements, commands, decrees, and instructions.”
NLT.7: When the men who lived there asked Isaac about his wife, Rebekah, he said, “She is my sister.” He was afraid to say, “She is my wife.” He thought, “They will kill me to get her, because she is so beautiful.”
NLT.8: But some time later, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked out his window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah.
NLT.9: Immediately, Abimelech called for Isaac and exclaimed, “She is obviously your wife! Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” “Because I was afraid someone would kill me to get her from me,” Isaac replied.
NLT.10: “How could you do this to us?” Abimelech exclaimed. “One of my people might easily have taken your wife and slept with her, and you would have made us guilty of great sin.”
NLT.11: Then Abimelech issued a public proclamation: “Anyone who touches this man or his wife will be put to death!”
NLT.12: When Isaac planted his crops that year, he harvested a hundred times more grain than he planted, for the LORD blessed him.
NLT.13: He became a very rich man, and his wealth continued to grow.
NLT.14: He acquired so many flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and servants that the Philistines became jealous of him.
NLT.15: So the Philistines filled up all of Isaac’s wells with dirt. These were the wells that had been dug by the servants of his father, Abraham.
NLT.16: Finally, Abimelech ordered Isaac to leave the country. “Go somewhere else,” he said, “for you have become too powerful for us.”
NLT.17: So Isaac moved away to the Gerar Valley, where he set up their tents and settled down.
NLT.18: He reopened the wells his father had dug, which the Philistines had filled in after Abraham’s death. Isaac also restored the names Abraham had given them.
NLT.19: Isaac’s servants also dug in the Gerar Valley and discovered a well of fresh water.
NLT.20: But then the shepherds from Gerar came and claimed the spring. “This is our water,” they said, and they argued over it with Isaac’s herdsmen. So Isaac named the well Esek (which means “argument”).
NLT.21: Isaac’s men then dug another well, but again there was a dispute over it. So Isaac named it Sitnah (which means “hostility”).
NLT.22: Abandoning that one, Isaac moved on and dug another well. This time there was no dispute over it, so Isaac named the place Rehoboth (which means “open space”), for he said, “At last the LORD has created enough space for us to prosper in this land.”
NLT.23: From there Isaac moved to Beersheba,
NLT.24: where the LORD appeared to him on the night of his arrival. “I am the God of your father, Abraham,” he said. “Do not be afraid, for I am with you and will bless you. I will multiply your descendants, and they will become a great nation. I will do this because of my promise to Abraham, my servant.”
NLT.25: Then Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the LORD. He set up his camp at that place, and his servants dug another well.
NLT.26: One day King Abimelech came from Gerar with his adviser, Ahuzzath, and also Phicol, his army commander.
NLT.27: “Why have you come here?” Isaac asked. “You obviously hate me, since you kicked me off your land.”
NLT.28: They replied, “We can plainly see that the LORD is with you. So we want to enter into a sworn treaty with you. Let’s make a covenant.
NLT.29: Swear that you will not harm us, just as we have never troubled you. We have always treated you well, and we sent you away from us in peace. And now look how the LORD has blessed you!”
NLT.30: So Isaac prepared a covenant feast to celebrate the treaty, and they ate and drank together.
NLT.31: Early the next morning, they each took a solemn oath not to interfere with each other. Then Isaac sent them home again, and they left him in peace.
NLT.32: That very day Isaac’s servants came and told him about a new well they had dug. “We’ve found water!” they exclaimed.
NLT.33: So Isaac named the well Shibah (which means “oath”). And to this day the town that grew up there is called Beersheba (which means “well of the oath”).
NLT.34: At the age of forty, Esau married two Hittite wives: Judith, the daughter of Beeri, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon.
NLT.35: But Esau’s wives made life miserable for Isaac and Rebekah.

NRSVCE.1: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Gerar, to King Abimelech of the Philistines.
NRSVCE.2: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt; settle in the land that I shall show you.
NRSVCE.3: Reside in this land as an alien, and I will be with you, and will bless you; for to you and to your descendants I will give all these lands, and I will fulfill the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.
NRSVCE.4: I will make your offspring as numerous as the stars of heaven, and will give to your offspring all these lands; and all the nations of the earth shall gain blessing for themselves through your offspring,
NRSVCE.5: because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
NRSVCE.7: When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, “She is my sister”; for he was afraid to say, “My wife,” thinking, “or else the men of the place might kill me for the sake of Rebekah, because she is attractive in appearance.”
NRSVCE.8: When Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech of the Philistines looked out of a window and saw him fondling his wife Rebekah.
NRSVCE.9: So Abimelech called for Isaac, and said, “So she is your wife! Why then did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I thought I might die because of her.”
NRSVCE.10: Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”
NRSVCE.11: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever touches this man or his wife shall be put to death.”
NRSVCE.12: Isaac sowed seed in that land, and in the same year reaped a hundredfold. The LORD blessed him,
NRSVCE.13: and the man became rich; he prospered more and more until he became very wealthy.
NRSVCE.14: He had possessions of flocks and herds, and a great household, so that the Philistines envied him.
NRSVCE.15: (Now the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham.)
NRSVCE.16: And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us; you have become too powerful for us.”
NRSVCE.17: So Isaac departed from there and camped in the valley of Gerar and settled there.
NRSVCE.18: Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of his father Abraham; for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham; and he gave them the names that his father had given them.
NRSVCE.19: But when Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found there a well of spring water,
NRSVCE.20: the herders of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herders, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the well Esek, because they contended with him.
NRSVCE.21: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also; so he called it Sitnah.
NRSVCE.22: He moved from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it; so he called it Rehoboth, saying, “Now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”
NRSVCE.23: From there he went up to Beer-sheba.
NRSVCE.24: And that very night the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham; do not be afraid, for I am with you and will bless you and make your offspring numerous for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
NRSVCE.25: So he built an altar there, called on the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there. And there Isaac’s servants dug a well.
NRSVCE.26: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
NRSVCE.27: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and have sent me away from you?”
NRSVCE.28: They said, “We see plainly that the LORD has been with you; so we say, let there be an oath between you and us, and let us make a covenant with you
NRSVCE.29: so that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and have done to you nothing but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.”
NRSVCE.30: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
NRSVCE.31: In the morning they rose early and exchanged oaths; and Isaac set them on their way, and they departed from him in peace.
NRSVCE.32: That same day Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water!”
NRSVCE.33: He called it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beer-sheba to this day.
NRSVCE.34: When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite;
NRSVCE.35: and they made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.

NET.1: There was a famine in the land, subsequent to the earlier famine that occurred in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.
NET.2: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt; settle down in the land that I will point out to you.
NET.3: Stay in this land. Then I will be with you and will bless you, for I will give all these lands to you and to your descendants, and I will fulfill the solemn promise I made to your father Abraham.
NET.4: I will multiply your descendants so they will be as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands. All the nations of the earth will pronounce blessings on one another using the name of your descendants.
NET.5: All this will come to pass because Abraham obeyed me and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”

NET.9: So Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, “She is really your wife! Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac replied, “Because I thought someone might kill me to get her.”

NET.12: When Isaac planted in that land, he reaped in the same year a hundred times what he had sown, because the LORD blessed him.

NET.16: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Leave us and go elsewhere, for you have become much more powerful than we are.”
NET.17: So Isaac left there and settled in the Gerar Valley.
NET.18: Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug back in the days of his father Abraham, for the Philistines had stopped them up after Abraham died. Isaac gave these wells the same names his father had given them.
NET.19: When Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and discovered a well with fresh flowing water there,
NET.20: the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water belongs to us!” So Isaac named the well Esek because they argued with him about it.
NET.21: His servants dug another well, but they quarreled over it too, so Isaac named it Sitnah.
NET.22: Then he moved away from there and dug another well. They did not quarrel over it, so Isaac named it Rehoboth, saying, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will prosper in the land.”

NET.27: Isaac asked them, “Why have you come to me? You hate me and sent me away from you.”
